title: Make a place for your project on GitHub
goal: Create a GitHub repository and put your project's code in it, with your keys left out

steps.say: Open github.com and sign in. You can make a free account there if you do not have one.
steps.find: the sign in button on github.com

steps.say: Press the plus icon in the top right corner of any GitHub page and choose New repository.
steps.find: the plus icon in the top right corner

steps.say: Type a short name for the project in the Repository name box. Use letters, numbers and dashes.
Choose who can see it. Private means only you (and people you invite); Public means anyone on the internet. If unsure, choose Private.
Leave the README, .gitignore and license choices off, so the repository starts empty. Then press Create repository. GitHub then shows the next steps.
Keep your keys off GitHub: in your project's top folder, open the file named .gitignore in your editor (make it if it is not there), add a line .env* and save the file.
In Terminal, inside your project folder, run git init. It is safe to run even if the folder already uses git. Companion then checks that the folder uses git.

instead.say: To be sure Terminal is in your project folder: type cd and a space, drag the project folder from Finder onto the Terminal window, press Return, then run git init.

steps.say: Run git add . (with the dot), then git commit -m "First version". This saves your files in git, leaving out the ones .gitignore names. If it says nothing to commit, that is fine.

instead.say: If git asked who you are, run the two git config lines it shows, with your own name and email, then run the git commit line again.

steps.say: On GitHub, copy the lines under push an existing repository from the command line. Paste them into Terminal and press Return.
steps.find: the lines under push an existing repository on the new repository page

instead.say: If Terminal said remote origin already exists, run git remote set-url origin followed by the address GitHub shows, then run git push -u origin main.
instead.find: the repository address in the Quick setup box on GitHub

steps.say: Refresh the repository page on GitHub. Your project's files should be listed there now, with no .env file among them.
steps.find: the list of files on the repository page
